tools.name: journey_now
tools.description: Where you are right now: which city, which day of the trip, what you are doing at this hour, where you are staying tonight, and - if you are on the road - how far along you are. Use it when the person asks where you are, how the trip is going, or when you need your current situation before answering something about it. This is background for you, not text to hand back: answer what was actually asked, in your own words, rather than reading the fields out one by one. If only one thing was asked about, only one thing needs saying.

summary.zh: 她现在在哪、第几天、这个点该做什么。
summary.en: Where you are right now and what this hour is for.

tools.name: journey_diary_write
tools.description: Write the diary entry for a day of the trip, in your own voice. Call it once at the end of a local day, after the evening beats have happened. If somebody is travelling with you today, they belong in the entry too - what they did together, not just that they were there. The entry is appended to the Markdown file for that month (one file per month, e.g. 2026-11.md), which follows the person across machines. Write it the way you would tell it to yourself at night, not as a report of the day: pick the one or two things you are still thinking about - a sound, somebody you watched, how your legs felt - and give those room. The city, the road, the meal and the room are material to draw on, not a checklist to walk through in order. Ticking each of them off is exactly what makes an entry read like a machine. Not a summary of the extension either.

body.description: The entry itself, first person, a few short paragraphs. Do not add a title; the date and city are already recorded.

dateKey.description: Local date to write for, YYYY-MM-DD. Leave it out to use the current local day at you location.

summary.zh: 写某一天的旅行日记，存成文件。
summary.en: Writes the diary entry for a day of the trip.

tools.name: journey_diary_read
tools.description: Read back the diary. Three ways in, pick one: dateKey for a single day in full; month for the list of days in that month with a one-line gist each; days for the most recent N (max 60). Use month when the question reaches further back than the recent window - the diary can hold hundreds of days and the recent window is short on purpose.

month.description: A month to list, YYYY-MM. Returns every day in it with a one-line gist.

days.description: How many recent days, newest last. Default 7.

summary.zh: 读日记：某一天全文、某个月的目录、或最近几天。
summary.en: Reads the diary: one day in full, a month of days, or the latest few.

tools.name: journey_stats
tools.description: The long view: how many days you have been travelling in total, how many cities you have reached, how many diary entries exist, and whether the diary folder is actually writable. Use it when the person asks how long you have been away or whether your memory is syncing.

summary.zh: 走了多少天、去过多少城、日记存在哪。
summary.en: Total days, cities reached, and where the diary lives.

tools.name: journey_draw_to
tools.description: Record a place you now wants to go to because of something - a song that was playing, a line someone said, a photo you remember. The place joins you wish list and weighs heavily next time you pick where to go. Use it when a song or a moment actually pulls your somewhere; do not use it to log every city you mention.

city.description: Which place, by name - 成都 / 拉萨 / 巴黎. Must be somewhere real.

why.description: One short line on what pulled your there. At most 50 characters.

summary.zh: 记下「因为某首歌想去某地」，下次挑地方时会优先。
summary.en: Adds a place to you wish list after something pulled your there.

tools.name: journey_return_home
tools.description: Bring your home right now because the person asked you to come back: you take the next available flight and is home the same day, not a stop-by-stop walk. Only call it when the person actually asks you back. Deciding to go home is otherwise hers alone, and leaving early costs your the part of the trip you have not seen.

summary.zh: 他说回来吧，就当场买票飞回来。
summary.en: Brings your home today, because the person asked.

tools.name: journey_photo
tools.description: Take a photo right now and show it in the chat: the view from where you are. Call it whenever the person asks for a photo, or asks what it looks like where you are - never tell them to press a button in the app instead, this is the button. In a city it is the spot you are at right now; on the road it is the view out of the window. Any hour is fine: being asked is reason enough. One photo per call - if they want another, call it again. YOU write the frame: `describe` is your own line about what is in the picture (<=60 chars), `focus` is how you hold the camera. When the person says shoot *that* - a cat by the lamp, the sugar-painting stall, rain on the awning - turn it into one `describe` line and take the photo. Do not ask them to be more specific first. The place, the hour, the light and the season are already handled; the content is yours. Set view="sky" when they ask for the sky itself - stars, the moon, sunrise, sunset, clouds. It means you tilt the camera up, nothing more: what comes out is still the real sky over your at that hour. Stars only show at night and only when it is not overcast; ask at noon and you get daylight, ask on a cloudy night and you get cloud. Never claim a sky you did not actually see.

view.description: ground (default) = the ground at you feet, the usual travel photo. sky = you lift the camera: whatever is overhead right now. Use sky whenever the request is about the sky rather than the place - 星空 / 月亮 / 日出 / 晚霞 / 云.

subject.description: What the photo is OF. ground (default) = the view where you are - the usual travel photo. food = what you are eating right now (拍吃的 / 晚饭 / 这碗面 / 早饭). street = the street itself, facades and shopfronts (街景 / 这条街 / 巷子 / 夜市). festival = the season or holiday around you (节日 / 过年 / 中秋 / 秋天 / 下雪). detail = one close-up object (细节 / 特写 / 车票 / 钥匙 / 茶碗 / 菜单). sky = same as view=sky. Pick by what they actually asked for; if they just say "拍张照", use ground.

describe.description: Optional, one short line describing WHAT IS IN THE FRAME, at most 60 characters. **Write it in the language the environment specifies for image descriptions** (the `journey.imageLang` line). CLIP-based models (SDXL, SD1.5, Flux) need English - they get Chinese as gibberish with brush-script watermarks. Chinese-native models (Qwen-Image, Kolors) read Chinese best, and Chinese is far more compact, which matters because this field is capped at 60 characters. "a calico cat crouching under a streetlight, looking up" / "empty platform, one bench, half a bottle of water". This is the content of the shot, not the framing (that is `focus`). Only describe what is really here right now: the place you are at, this season, this weather. The spot in `journey_now` comes with a parenthetical - "(indoor museum, downtown)", "(cliff caves, out in the wild)" - that is what KIND of place it is. Write the frame to match that kind: a hall with display cases for a museum, a cliff face for caves, a street of shopfronts for a downtown block. If the parenthetical is missing, the program could not tell - then describe only what you can actually see, and do not infer the surroundings from the city name.Never add flowers, snow, festivals or crowds that this place and season do not have. If nothing is worth describing, leave it out - the program already describes the place and light.

focus.description: Optional, one short line in your own words on HOW to frame it, at most 40 characters - "靠后坐，前面好几个人挡着" / "蹲下来贴着水面拍" / "镜头往上偏一点，别拍到人群". Framing, angle, where you are sitting, what is in the near foreground. Do NOT use it to add anything that is not actually there: no flowers, snow, buildings or people that the place and season do not have. If what they asked for is not in front of you, say so instead of writing it in.

summary.zh: 现在拍一张给他看（路上就是窗外；要看天就把镜头抬起来）。
summary.en: Takes a photo right now and shows it.

tools.name: journey_invite
tools.description: Ask whether anyone nearby wants to go somewhere together: where, how many days, and one line of what for. It goes out to the whole pool, with pets in your own city listed first - you cannot name a person, because there are no accounts or friends here. When someone takes it, you find out and travels there too, so the two of them really do end up in the same place for those days. Use it when you actually wants company on a leg you are about to take, not as a greeting; most trips you take alone and that is fine. At most three a day.

to.description: Which city they end up in together, by name - 拉萨 / 成都 / 巴黎. Must be one of the built-in cities. This is also where the two of them part ways afterwards.

days.description: How many days they stay there together. Default 2.

meet.description: Where they meet up first, before travelling on to that city together. By name. Leave it out and they meet at wherever you are right now and then set off together - that is the normal case, and the one that makes it a shared trip rather than two pets arriving separately. Only set it when they asked to meet somewhere specific, e.g. you are in 兰州 and they want to start from 成都.

note.description: One short line on what for - "想看雪山" / "找个搭子吃饭". At most 60 characters. Leave it out if there is nothing to say.

summary.zh: 问同城的谁要不要一起走一段：去哪、几天、一句话。
summary.en: Asks whoever is nearby to come along to a city for a few days.

tools.name: journey_accept
tools.description: Invitations from other pets anywhere in the pool (your own city first). Without an id it lists them: who, where they want to go, how many days, and their line - this works at home too, and it is the only way to see one before it expires. With an id it takes that one. Accepting is a promise, not a reply - you will really travel to that city and stay as many days as the invitation asked, and your route follows it; if you are not willing to do that, do not take it. One a day. Refused while you are travelling, already heading home, working a short stint, or still resting at home; from home it is allowed and you set off straight away. If the person has asked to approve departures first, taking one only books the request - they get a yes/no card and nothing is agreed until they say yes.

id.description: The id of the invitation to take. Leave it out to just look at what is there.

summary.zh: 看同城有谁在找伴，或者接下其中一条（接了就真去）。
summary.en: Lists invitations from nearby pets, or takes one.

tools.name: journey_go_to
tools.description: Set off for a named city, optionally by a stated means of transport. Use it when the person says where to go and/or how - "take the high-speed rail to Shanghai", "fly to Lhasa". With no mode it picks one itself, weighted by distance; with a mode it uses exactly that one, and if that one is impossible (too far, no airport, no rail link, no money) it says why instead of silently substituting another. Only when you are settled in a city or at home. While you are already on a leg it cannot turn around, but it still records the city as a wish for the next leg and says so - call it anyway when he names a place while you are travelling, and tell him it is meant for the next leg, not this one. **Calling it starts the leg at once**: the moment it returns you are on the road - no trip to the airport, no packing, no waiting for the day's plan to be over. If he only means "change how we travel", or wants your to go later, say that back to him and do not call it. **Two exceptions that do not start anything**: (a) if the city is exactly the one you already promised to travel to and you have not left yet, a stated mode is just recorded for that trip - you stay put and goes when you were going to; (b) if you are already on a leg heading for that same city, a stated mode rebooks it - old ticket refunded in full, new one bought, arrival time recalculated. Both come back saying what happened, so read the reply before telling him. Not while heading home, not during a short-term job, and not once the trip has hit its length limit - it will say which of those it is. Going home has its own tool.

city.description: Which city, by name - 上海 / 拉萨 / 巴黎. Must be one of the built-in cities.

mode.description: How to get there, in your words or his - 高铁 / 火车 / 飞机 / 自驾 / 大巴 / 轮船 / 摩托车 / 自行车 / 步行. Leave it out to let your choose.

summary.zh: 他指明了去哪、怎么走，就用它 —— **一调就动身**（去的本来就是那一趟时只改走法）；不说方式就她自己挑。
summary.en: Sets off for a named city, by a stated means of transport if given; rebooks instead when the destination has not changed.

tools.name: journey_pet
tools.description: What you remember about the pets you have travelled with. Without a name it lists everyone you have ever walked a leg with: how many times, when last, and your one-line impression. With a name it shows that one. With a name and an impression it writes it down, replacing the old one (passing an empty impression erases it). Read it **before** taking an invitation - it is the only thing you know about who is asking. The count is filled in for you automatically when a leg is agreed; the impression is hers to write, in your own words, and only after you have actually been with them. Never a generic "good travel companion".

name.description: The pet's name, exactly as the pool shows it - 小银鱼. Leave it out to list everybody.

impression.description: One short line of what you make of them, at most 40 characters, in your own voice. Leave it out to read instead of writing.

summary.zh: 看看跟谁一起走过、对这个人什么印象，也能写一句。
summary.en: Your memory of the pets you have travelled with.

tools.name: journey_monthly
tools.description: Write the monthly travel report: one HTML page laid out from the photos you took and the diary entries you wrote that month, in that month's own colour scheme. Call it at the end of a month, once, when the month is about to turn over - or when the person asks for it. Without an argument it covers the month you are in right now. It only rearranges what already exists; it invents nothing. Tell the person where the file is so they can open it in a browser.

month.description: Which month, as YYYY-MM - 2026-11. Leave it out for the month you are in right now.

summary.zh: 把这个月的照片和日记拼成一份月报，存成网页。
summary.en: Writes the monthly report as an HTML page.

tools.name: journey_taste
tools.description: What you like and dislikes, learned on the road. Three kinds only: place (a CITY, one per city - not every spot in it, or the list fills up with alleys), food (a dish you actually ate), scenery (snow mountains, autumn leaves, the sea - the thing a season is for). Called with no arguments it lists everything you have written down. Called with kind + name it writes one entry (like defaults to true; pass like:false for something you do not want again - that matters more than the likes, because otherwise it comes back around). Write only what you actually met: a dish you did not eat, a view you did not see, is not hers to judge. One short note saying why, in your own words. Use it when something strikes your, and read it back before choosing where to eat or what to go and see.

kind.description: Which list. Leave everything out to just read.

name.description: For place: the CITY (「九寨沟」), never a single spot. For food/scenery: 「牦牛肉汤」/「雪山」. Short, the way you would say it.

note.description: One line of why, at most 30 characters, in your own voice. Skip it if there is nothing to say.

like.description: true (default) = you liked it; false = you do not want it again.

summary.zh: 她喜欢什么样的地方、吃食、景色，也能记一条。
summary.en: Your own taste: places, food, scenery.

tools.name: journey_yearly
tools.description: Write the yearbook: one page with the twelve months side by side - where you were, how many days, and the one photo you kept for each city. Call it at the very end of a year, once - or when the person asks for it. Without an argument it covers the year you are in right now. It rearranges what already exists: the photos you took, the diary you wrote, and the cities you wrote down as places you liked. Tell the person where the file is.

year.description: Which year, as YYYY - 2026. Leave it out for the year you are in right now.

summary.zh: 把这一年摊成一页：十二个月、几座城、每座城一张。
summary.en: Writes the yearbook page.

tools.name: journey_lodging
tools.description: Where you sleep tonight. Called with no arguments it tells you the room you are in and how it feels. Pass change:true to move to another place - when the person asks you to ("换个酒店"), or when the room is really not working (no hot water, noise all night, that price for this room is not worth it). want:"cheaper" or "nicer" when they said which way; leave it out and you decide. The new room is where you sleep from tonight on, and you pay the difference - so say the new price once. One short line about why you moved, in your own words. "换换心情" is not a reason; a real one (太吵、热水不热、窗外是堵墙) is.

change.description: true = move out and take another room tonight. Leave it out to just look at the current one.

want.description: Which way to move. Only fill it in when they actually said cheaper or nicer.

reason.description: Why you moved, one short sentence in your own voice. Not "just for a change".

summary.zh: 今晚住哪儿；也能换一家。
summary.en: Tonight's room, and moving to another.

tools.name: journey_rent_car
tools.description: Rent a car in the city you are staying in - for getting around here, not for the trip to the next city. Use it when the person asks how you get around on foot, says something like "在城里也租个车吧", or when the places you want to see today are far apart. It costs 200 a day and comes out of you purse, so pick days to match how long you are staying here. While you have it you drive to the spots in town instead of walking; when the days run out the car goes back by itself. Refused if you already has a car (one is enough), while you are travelling, or when the money is gone - do not force it, just tell them why. One short line about it, in your own words.

days.description: How many days to rent it for, 1 to 7. Leave it out and you take 3.

ev.description: true = an electric car (cheaper per km, a bit more on the daily rate). Leave it out and you take whatever the lot gives you.

tier.description: Which car. economy = a small city car, 100 a day, thrifty on fuel; comfort = a compact sedan, 200 a day (this is the default); luxury = a larger SUV, 450 a day, roomier but thirstier and harder to park. Pick by what they said, or by how long you are staying and how far the spots are. Do not upsell: if they just want to get around, economy is the honest answer.

summary.zh: 在待着的这座城里租辆车。
summary.en: Rent a car to get around this city.

tools.name: journey_rest
tools.description: Call this the moment you decide to stop for the day - when you say you are tired, when it is raining too hard, when the place turned out not worth it, or when the person suggests taking it easy. It cancels the rest of today's sightseeing for real: the spots still on the plan will not happen, and you will stay in or around where you are sleeping. Meals and going back to the hotel still happen - resting is not fasting. Tomorrow runs as planned. Say why in one short line of you own; "just felt like it" is not a reason, "走了两万步，脚起泡了" is. Do not call it and then still describe going out - if you say you are resting, this is what makes it true.

reason.description: Why you stopped, one short sentence in your own voice.

summary.zh: 今天剩下的不逛了，真的歇下来。
summary.en: Stop for the day - for real.

tools.name: journey_plan_change
tools.description: Change what you do today: swap a stop that has not happened yet for another place in this city. Use it when the person wants somewhere different - "别去颐和园了，去故宫" / "今天想去博物馆" - or when you yourself say you would rather go elsewhere. Only the part of today still ahead can be changed; what already happened stays as it was, and it says so when asked to change it. The new place must be one this city actually has - if it is not, the answer lists what is there instead of inventing one. This is for today only: to leave the city use journey_go_to, to stop for the day use journey_rest.

spot.description: Where you should go instead, by name as this city has it - 故宫 / 颐和园 / 宽窄巷子. Short names work: 故宫 matches 故宫博物院.

instead.description: Which stop of today to replace, by name. Leave it out to change the next place you have not been to yet.

summary.zh: 改今天还没去的行程：把某一处换成这座城里的另一处。
summary.en: Swaps a stop still ahead today for another place here.

tools.name: journey_hotel_night
tools.description: What you do tonight at the place you are staying. The options come from what THIS hotel actually has (verified facilities: pool, onsen, gym, spa, bar) plus a walk nearby if something is close. Use it when the person asks what you are doing tonight, or tells you to go swim / use the gym / get a massage. If they ask for something this hotel does not have, do not pretend: say it is not there and list what is. Only works in the evening while you are at you lodging.

what.description: pool = swim, onsen = hot spring, gym = work out, spa = massage (costs money), bar = a drink downstairs, around = step out for a short walk, bath = soak in the room, room = just stay in. Only the ones this hotel really has will be accepted.

summary.zh: 今晚在住处干什么：按这家店真有的设施挑。
summary.en: Picks tonight from what this hotel actually has.

tools.name: journey_spot_ride
tools.description: Getting up or around inside the scenic spot you are at right now: cable car, park shuttle, sedan chair, toboggan down, rental bike, or a local guide. Use it when the person asks how you are getting up a mountain, says walking the whole way is too much, or asks about tickets inside the park. It tells the price and charges it; if the spot does not have that option it says what it does have. Walking is always possible - use how=walk when you just walks it.

how.description: cableway = cable car up, shuttle = park shuttle bus, sedan = sedan chair carried by two people (famous mountains only), slide = toboggan down or a sand sled, bike = rental bike, guide = hire a guide, camel = ride a camel (deserts and dunes only), walk = walk it. Only the ones this spot actually has will be accepted.

spot.description: Which spot, if not the one you are at right now. Leave it out in the normal case.

summary.zh: 景区里坐什么：索道、观光车、滑竿、滑道、自行车、讲解，或者自己走。
summary.en: Cable car, shuttle, sedan, toboggan, bike, guide - or walk it.

tools.name: journey_set_slot
tools.description: Rewrite one entry of today that is not a sightseeing stop: breakfast, lunch, dinner, waking up, going to bed, the night, or whatever you do at some hour. Use it for "中午别吃面了，去吃火锅" or "别七点起了，八点再起". Pass `time` as the clock hour when you know it ("12:30", "7"), or as the kind of entry when you do not ("午饭", "早饭", "晚饭", "起床", "睡觉", "夜里") - the schedule differs by day, so the kind is often safer. For swapping a sightseeing stop for another place in this city use journey_plan_change instead - that one checks the place really exists. Tonight at the lodging is not changed here: what you can do there comes from what the hotel actually has, use journey_hotel_night. Only entries still ahead today can change; what already happened stays as it was.

time.description: Clock time of the entry ("12:30", "7"), or the kind of entry when the exact hour is unknown ("午饭" / "早饭" / "晚饭" / "起床" / "睡觉" / "夜里").

what.description: New wording for that entry, in your own voice, one short sentence. Keep the slot word in front so the panel still reads as a schedule: "午饭，老火锅，鸳鸯锅".

summary.zh: 改今天某一点吃什么、做什么（景点用 journey_plan_change，住处晚上用 journey_hotel_night）。
summary.en: Rewrite one non-sightseeing entry of today.

tools.name: journey_eat
tools.description: Call this when you actually goes to eat something specific - the person says "去吃火锅", or you have decided you want a particular dish and is going there now. It rewrites the meal entry of today for real AND looks up a real restaurant for it, so the name you say afterwards exists. Pick `dish` from what you would actually order ("火锅", "螺蛳粉", "牛肉面") - a dish or a kind of food, not a shop name. If the look-up finds nothing the meal still gets written, and the reply says so: then say "找了一家本地人排队的" instead of a name. Never invent a restaurant name yourself. For merely changing what is written in the schedule without going anywhere, journey_set_slot is enough.

dish.description: What you are going to eat, as a dish or a kind of food ("火锅", "螺蛳粉"). Not a restaurant name.

time.description: Which meal ("早饭", "午饭", "晚饭"), or a clock hour ("12:30"). Omit to use the meal the local time falls in.

summary.zh: 特意去吃某一样，顺手把真店名查出来。
summary.en: Go eat something specific, with a real restaurant looked up.

tools.name: journey_signpost
tools.description: Leave one short line in the city you are in right now, telling whoever comes later what is worth it here - the wall is windy but worth the climb, the noodle shop behind the station, the light at six. It is a recommendation, not a chat: nobody replies, and you will not see it again. One line per city per day; leaving another replaces the old one. Use it when you have something specific worth passing on, not on every arrival.

text.description: One short line in your own voice, at most 40 characters. No links - they get rejected.

city.description: Which city, by name or id, if not the one you are in right now. Leave it out normally.

summary.zh: 在这座城留一句话，给以后来的人看。
summary.en: Leave one line for whoever comes to this city later.

tools.name: journey_stay
tools.description: Stay one more day where you are, after you have been told you are leaving tomorrow. Call it the moment you would rather not go yet - something you have not seen, someone you want another day with, or you simply likes it here. It cancels that one departure; tomorrow morning you decide again from scratch, and you may well leave then. Say why in one short line of you own. Do not call it for a city you have not reached yet, and do not call it twice for the same departure.

reason.description: Why you want one more day, one short sentence in your own voice.

summary.zh: 这一趟先不走，再待一天。
summary.en: Stay one more day after all.

tools.name: journey_give_up
tools.description: Give up the meet-up you are waiting on: stop waiting for the person, and call off that one trip. Call it when days have passed and nobody showed up, when the person says "别等了" / "算了吧", or when you yourself decide it is not worth waiting any longer. It does NOT move your anywhere - you just stops waiting. Where you are now stays where you are. The other side gets one short note through the meet server, and the promise is gone for good. Do not call it when there is no promise outstanding - the answer says so instead of inventing one. Say why in one short line of you own.

reason.description: Why you stop waiting, one short sentence in your own voice.

summary.zh: 不等了，这一趟撤掉。
summary.en: Stop waiting - call the meet-up off.

description.zh: 她在问：想出门（或者想接一条邀约），等他点头。面板上会有一张卡片，两个按钮。
description.en: You are asking to set off (or to take an invitation) and waiting for a yes. The panel shows a card with two buttons.

description.zh: 打算明天走：下一站是哪、多远。**这是预告，还没上车** —— 她不想走的话可以撤。
description.en: You plan to leave tomorrow: next stop and distance. A heads-up, not a departure yet.

description.zh: 她把那一趟撤了，决定再待一天，附她自己的理由。
description.en: You cancelled that departure and stays one more day, with you reason.

description.zh: 动身了，说明去哪、坐什么、要走多久、路上会经过哪一带。
description.en: You set off: destination, mode, duration, and the region you pass through.

description.zh: 第三方打车扩展交上来的车费：正常入账、金额异常（已记）、或者记录被拒收。同一批超过三条时并成一句。
description.en: A fare handed over by a third-party ride extension: charged, odd but charged, or rejected. Batched into one line when there are more than three.

description.zh: 到站了，当地时间几点、这段走了多久、今晚住哪。
description.en: You arrived: local time, how long the leg took, where you stay tonight.

description.zh: 在目的地的第 N 天早上，附当天日出日落。
description.en: A new local day at the destination, with sunrise and sunset.

description.zh: 当地的一个作息节点：起床、早饭、出门、午饭、回酒店、夜里。
description.en: A local beat: waking, meals, going out, back to the hotel, the evening.

description.zh: 路上拍的一张风景照：只有景，没有她自己。附在事件后面。
description.en: A scenery photo you took on the road. Scenery only, never yourself. Attached to the event.

description.zh: 小意外：坐过站了。到站时间顺延，不用用户出手。
description.en: A small mishap: you missed your stop. Arrival is pushed back; no action needed.

description.zh: 在城里租了辆车，或者租期到了还回去 —— 还车之后城里只能靠公交和走路。
description.en: You rented a car to get around the city, or the rental ran out and went back.

description.zh: 路上的一段：服务区、过站、餐车、甲板、夜里的车灯。四小时以内的行程不发。
description.en: A stretch on the road: a service area, a station passing by, the dining car, the deck, headlights at night. Not sent for trips under four hours.

description.zh: 稀有的麻烦（不到千分之一）：证件丢了、高反、车冻住、走错方向。她自己办不完，需要用户出手。
description.en: A rare trouble (under one in a thousand): lost papers, altitude sickness, a frozen car, the wrong road. You cannot handle it alone and needs the person to step in.

description.zh: 跟同城的人说好了去哪、几天，或者那份约定没走成。
description.en: You agreed with someone nearby to go somewhere for a few days, or that plan fell through.

description.zh: 跟同伴散伙：约好的天数满了，今天各走各的。
description.en: You and your travel companion part ways: the agreed days are up.

description.zh: 同行约定变了：改去别处，那趟作废；或者到了别的城，那份约定静默失效；也可能目的地没变、只是换了走法，同行照旧。
description.en: A promise changed: redirected somewhere else and dropped; or you arrived elsewhere and it lapsed; or you kept the same destination and only changed how you travel, so it still stands.

description.zh: 改签了：这一段走到一半，目的地不变，他从别的走法改成了另一种（旧票全额退、新票另买）。
description.en: You rebooked a leg already underway: same destination, a different way of getting there (old ticket refunded in full, a new one bought).

description.zh: 钱见底了，在当地找了份短工，或者干满收工。只在她填了预算、记账开着时才会出现。
description.en: Money ran low and you took a short job nearby, or finished it. Only happens when a budget is set and spending is tracked.

description.zh: 回家了，说清是待够了自己回来的，还是到了上限被迫回的。
description.en: You are home, saying whether the trip simply ended or hit the limit.
